red_flags: chest pain spreading to arm or jaw
records.source: NHS website: Heartburn and acid reflux / Indigestion - verify
records.description: Acidity / indigestion. Common words people use: acidity, heartburn, gas, burning chest, indigestion, jalan, seene mein jalan, teza.
Common skin condition with spots, blackheads and pimples on the face, chest and back, mostly in teenagers and young adults.
red_flags: acne with irregular periods or excess hair
records.age_notes: Teenager: Dermatologist or Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Acne with irregular periods or excess hair growth in women: see Gynecologist for PCOS check.
baseline_tests: Hormone tests if irregular periods or excess hair
Further tests only when another underlying cause is suspected

red_flags: swelling of lips tongue face or throat
records.age_notes: Children with suspected food or medicine allergy should be assessed by a pediatric clinician; severe reactions require emergency care.
records.description: Allergic reaction. Common words people use: allergy, allergic reaction, hives, urticaria, itchy rash, food allergy, medicine allergy, allergy reaction.
Chest tightness or pain, brought on by effort or stress and relieved by rest, caused by reduced blood flow to the heart muscle.
records.age_notes: Mostly adults over 40.
baseline_tests: Stress test or echocardiogram if advised

records.description: Ongoing feelings of worry or fear that are hard to control, with restlessness, poor sleep, tension and sometimes a racing heart.
red_flags: panic attacks that do not settle
unable to function at work or home
records.age_notes: Children and teenagers: Child Psychiatrist or Pediatrician.

records.description: Inflamed appendix causing pain that starts near the belly button and moves to the lower right, with nausea and fever. Usually needs surgery.
red_flags: severe pain in lower right abdomen
pain that gets worse when moving or coughing
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician or Pediatric Surgeon.
records.gender_notes: Women: a Gynecologist may also assess to rule out other causes.

records.description: Long-term lung condition causing wheeze, cough, chest tightness and breathlessness, often worse at night or with dust, cold air or exercise.
red_flags: inability to speak normally because of breathlessness
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician or child lung specialist.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy requires review of asthma control and treatment by a clinician.
baseline_tests: Spirometry or another breathing test when appropriate

records.description: Long-term skin condition causing dry, itchy, red and cracked skin, often in skin folds. Common in children and tends to flare up and settle.
red_flags: skin weeping, crusting or very painful
no response to moisturiser and cream
records.age_notes: Baby or child: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: Additional testing only if another diagnosis or infection is suspected

records.description: Very common problem, usually from muscle or joint strain, that often improves within weeks. Staying active helps recovery.
red_flags: numbness around the genitals or buttocks
loss of bladder or bowel control
pain after a fall or injury
records.age_notes: Child with back pain: Pediatrician. Adults over 50 with new severe pain: see doctor soon.
baseline_tests: Vitamin D and calcium tests if advised
X-ray or MRI only if the doctor advises
records.source: NHS: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/back-pain/ | NHS website: Back pain - verify

records.age_notes: Child with breathing difficulty: urgent Pediatrician or Emergency.
records.source: NHS website: Shortness of breath / Asthma - verify
records.description: Breathing difficulty. Common words people use: shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, wheezing, asthma, saans phoolna, saans lene mein dikkat.

red_flags: burn on face genitals or buttocks
records.age_notes: Children with burns should receive prompt clinical assessment; young children can deteriorate with significant burns.
baseline_tests: Clinical assessment of burn depth and extent
Blood tests or imaging only when clinically indicated for significant burns
records.description: Burn / scald injury. Common words people use: burn, scald, hot water burn, thermal burn, chemical burn, jalna, jal gaya.
Infection of the airways or lungs causing cough with phlegm, wheeze and breathlessness. Mild cases clear on their own; severe cases need treatment.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. Older adults: see doctor soon.

red_flags: pain spreading to arm, jaw or back
records.source: NHS website: Chest pain / Heart attack - verify
records.description: Chest pain (possible heart problem). Common words people use: chest pain, chest tightness, pain in left arm, seene mein dard.
Common viral illness in children with itchy red spots that turn into blisters, with mild fever. Most people recover in 1 to 2 weeks.
red_flags: rash that turns red, hot or very painful
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. Adults, newborns and people with weak immunity need doctor early.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women who are exposed should contact a Gynecologist urgently.

records.description: Long-term loss of kidney function, often linked to diabetes and high blood pressure. Early on it may have no symptoms; later causes swelling, tiredness and changes in urine.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician or pediatric kidney specialist.

red_flags: not starting to heal within 10 days
records.age_notes: A newborn exposed to an active cold sore requires urgent medical advice.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy warrants clinician advice if lesions are severe or recurrent.
baseline_tests: Swab or other testing only if the diagnosis is uncertain
records.description: Cold sore / oral herpes symptom. Common words people use: cold sore, lip blister, fever blister, tingling lip, itching lip, burning lip, honton par chhala.
Mild viral infection of the nose and throat with runny or blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat and mild cough. Usually gets better in 1 to 2 weeks without antibiotics.
records.age_notes: Baby under 3 months with fever or poor feeding: urgent Pediatrician. Child: Pediatrician.

records.description: Red, sore, watery or sticky eyes caused by infection or allergy. Usually settles in 1 to 2 weeks.
records.age_notes: Newborn with sticky eye: urgent Pediatrician. Child: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: Swab if severe or not improving
Eye swab only when clinically indicated, such as selected persistent or unusual infections

records.description: Difficulty passing stools or going less than 3 times a week. Usually due to low fibre, low fluids or lack of movement.
red_flags: unable to pass gas or stool
persistent vomiting or severe abdominal swelling
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. Baby with constipation: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Common in pregnancy; discuss with Gynecologist.
baseline_tests: Thyroid test and blood sugar if long-lasting
Blood tests or other investigations if persistent or another cause is suspected

records.description: Long-term lung disease, mostly in smokers, causing daily cough, phlegm and breathlessness that slowly gets worse.
records.age_notes: Mostly adults over 35.

red_flags: unexplained weight loss or night sweats
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: Usually none for a simple cold
Sputum test (if cough lasts over 2-3 weeks)
records.source: NHS website: Cough / Common cold - verify
records.description: Cough / cold / upper respiratory infection. Common words people use: cough, cold, runny nose, flu, khansi, nazla, zukam.
Viral infection with fever, cough, tiredness and sometimes loss of smell or taste. Most people recover at home but some become short of breath.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. Older adults and people with chronic disease have higher risk.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy can alter risk and treatment considerations; seek clinician advice when unwell.
baseline_tests: COVID PCR or rapid antigen test
COVID-19 diagnostic testing when clinically indicated
Oxygen saturation assessment when respiratory symptoms are present

records.description: Body loses more fluid than it takes in, often from heat, vomiting or diarrhoea. Causes thirst, dark urine, dizziness and tiredness.
records.age_notes: Baby or child: Pediatrician urgently. Older adults are at higher risk.

records.description: Mosquito-borne viral fever causing sudden high fever, severe body and joint pain, headache, pain behind the eyes and rash. A small number of people develop severe dengue with bleeding.
red_flags: fever settling but patient getting worse
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician early. Do not give aspirin or ibuprofen.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women: contact Gynecologist and doctor early.
baseline_tests: CBC with platelet count (repeat as advised)
Dengue laboratory testing as clinically indicated and according to illness timing
CBC / platelet count may be used to monitor illness severity
records.source: NHS: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/dengue/ | WHO: Dengue and severe dengue - https://www.who.int/health-topics/dengue-and-severe-dengue

records.description: Pocket of pus in the tooth or gum caused by infection, causing severe throbbing toothache, swelling, bad taste and fever.
red_flags: swelling of the face or neck
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatric Dentist or Pediatrician.

records.description: Persistent low mood, loss of interest and energy, sleep and appetite changes. It is a common, treatable illness.
red_flags: feeling that life is not worth living
unable to care for yourself or others
records.age_notes: Teenagers and children: Child Psychiatrist or Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Women after childbirth with low mood: Psychiatrist and Gynecologist.
baseline_tests: TSH and CBC to rule out medical causes
Vitamin B12 and D if advised

records.age_notes: Child with these symptoms: urgent Pediatrician.
records.description: Possible high blood sugar. Common words people use: excess thirst, frequent urination, weight loss, high sugar, bohat pyaas, sugar.
Dangerous emergency in people with diabetes when the body makes too many acids (ketones). Needs hospital treatment at once.
records.age_notes: Most common in children and young adults with type 1 diabetes.

red_flags: signs of dehydration (very dry mouth, no urine, dizziness)
symptoms in a baby or elderly person
lasting more than a few days
records.age_notes: Child or baby: Pediatrician, and dehydration can become serious quickly.
records.source: NHS website: Diarrhoea and vomiting - verify
records.description: Diarrhea / vomiting (gastroenteritis). Common words people use: diarrhea, vomiting, loose motions, food poisoning, dast, ulti, pait kharab.
Blood clot in a deep leg vein causing pain, swelling, warmth and redness, usually in one leg. The clot can travel to the lungs.
records.age_notes: Higher risk after long travel, surgery or bed rest.
records.gender_notes: Higher risk in pregnancy and with hormonal pills.

records.description: Infection of the middle or outer ear causing ear pain, sometimes fever, discharge or muffled hearing. Common in children and often settles in a few days.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician first.
baseline_tests: Hearing test if hearing loss persists

red_flags: swelling or pain behind the ear
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician or ENT.
records.description: Ear problem. Common words people use: ear pain, earache, ear discharge, hearing loss, kaan dard, kaan mein dard.

symptom_keywords: pait ke neeche ek taraf dard
پیٹ کے نیچے ایک طرف درد
records.description: Pregnancy that grows outside the womb, usually in a fallopian tube. It can cause severe one-sided belly pain and bleeding and is a life-threatening emergency.
red_flags: pain at the tip of the shoulder
records.age_notes: Applies to women of childbearing age.
records.gender_notes: Applies to women only.

records.description: Condition where abnormal brain activity causes repeated seizures (fits). A first seizure always needs medical review.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician or child neurologist. Fever fits in toddlers: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women with epilepsy need a Gynecologist and Neurologist together.

records.age_notes: Child: Pediatric Ophthalmologist if available.
records.source: NHS website: Red eye / Eye pain - verify
records.description: Eye problem. Common words people use: red eye, eye pain, watery eyes, blurred vision, aankh lal, aankh mein dard, aankh se pani.

records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. Elderly: see a doctor sooner.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women should see a doctor early.
records.source: NHS website: High temperature (fever) in adults - verify
records.description: Fever / possible infection. Common words people use: fever, high temperature, body ache, chills, bukhar.

red_flags: baby under 3 months with any fever
very sleepy or hard to wake
records.age_notes: Infants under 3 months with fever need urgent medical assessment.
records.source: NHS website: High temperature (fever) in children - verify
records.description: Fever in a child. Common words people use: child fever, baby fever, bachay ko bukhar, bukhar bacha.
Viral infection that comes on suddenly with fever, aching body, tiredness, dry cough and sore throat. Usually improves in about a week with rest and fluids.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. Older adults, pregnant women and people with chronic illness should see a doctor early.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women should see a Gynecologist or doctor early because flu can be more serious.
baseline_tests: Chest X-ray if breathless or chest signs
Influenza testing when clinically indicated, especially when the result would change management

records.description: Immune reaction to a food such as nuts, eggs, milk or shellfish. Can cause hives, swelling and vomiting, and rarely a life-threatening reaction (anaphylaxis).
red_flags: swelling of lips, tongue or throat
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: Allergy skin prick test or specific IgE

records.description: Illness from eating contaminated food causing vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach cramps and fever. Usually passes in a few days with fluids.
records.age_notes: Baby or young child: Pediatrician early. Older adults: see doctor early.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women: contact Gynecologist or doctor.
baseline_tests: Stool test if severe or persistent

records.description: Hard lumps in the gallbladder that cause sudden pain in the upper right belly, often after fatty meals, with nausea.
red_flags: severe pain for more than 5 hours
very dark urine and pale stools
pain spreading to the back with vomiting
records.age_notes: More common in adults over 40.
records.gender_notes: More common in women, especially during or after pregnancy.
baseline_tests: Blood tests when complications or liver/biliary disease are suspected

records.description: Inflammation of the stomach lining causing upper stomach pain, bloating, nausea and indigestion. Often linked to infection with H. pylori, painkillers or alcohol.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: H. pylori stool or breath test

records.description: Sudden, severe pain, redness and swelling in a joint, often the big toe, caused by uric acid crystals. Attacks last days to weeks.
red_flags: high fever with hot swollen joint
records.age_notes: Mostly adults.
records.gender_notes: More common in men and in women after menopause.
baseline_tests: Joint fluid examination may be required when diagnosis is uncertain or infection must be excluded

records.gender_notes: Applies to women only.
records.source: NHS website: Period problems / Pelvic pain - verify
records.description: Menstrual / pelvic problem. Common words people use: period pain, irregular periods, heavy bleeding, pelvic pain, mahwari, mahwari mein dard, pelvic dard.
Allergic reaction to pollen or dust causing sneezing, runny or blocked nose and itchy eyes, often seasonal.
red_flags: symptoms not controlled with allergy tablets
swelling of lips tongue or throat
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: Allergy skin prick test or IgE if advised
Allergy testing if the diagnosis or trigger is unclear and testing is clinically indicated
records.source: NHS: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/hay-fever/ | NHS: Hay fever - https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/hay-fever/

records.description: Blow or fall to the head. Most are minor but some cause concussion or bleeding in the brain that needs urgent checking.
red_flags: clear fluid or blood from nose or ear
records.age_notes: Child or baby with any head injury and vomiting or drowsiness: urgent Pediatrician or hospital.
baseline_tests: CT scan head if red flags

records.age_notes: Child with repeated headaches: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: Brain imaging only if the doctor advises
records.description: Headache. Common words people use: headache, head pain, migraine, sar dard, sar mein dard.

symptom_keywords: pain spreading to arm or jaw
records.description: Emergency where blood flow to the heart is blocked. Typical signs are chest pressure or pain that may spread to the arm, neck or jaw, with sweating and breathlessness.
red_flags: chest pain lasting more than 15 minutes
pain spreading to arm, neck or jaw
records.age_notes: Risk rises in men over 45 and women over 55.
records.gender_notes: Women may have less typical signs such as nausea, back or jaw pain and unusual tiredness.

records.description: Condition where the heart does not pump blood well. Causes breathlessness, tiredness and swollen ankles.
records.age_notes: Mostly adults over 50.
baseline_tests: Blood tests (CBC, kidney function, electrolytes, NT-proBNP)

records.description: Burning feeling in the chest or throat caused by stomach acid coming up. Common after meals or when lying down.
red_flags: chest pain with sweating or breathlessness
records.age_notes: Baby with reflux: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Common in pregnancy; discuss with Gynecologist.
baseline_tests: Upper GI endoscopy if red flags
H. pylori testing if clinically indicated
Endoscopy if persistent symptoms or alarm features warrant it

records.description: Long-term raised pressure in the arteries. Often has no symptoms but raises the risk of heart attack, stroke and kidney disease.
red_flags: severe headache with blood pressure above 180/120
records.age_notes: Rare in children: Pediatrician if found.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women with high blood pressure: urgent Gynecologist (risk of pre-eclampsia).
baseline_tests: Kidney function tests and urine test
Repeat or ambulatory/home blood pressure measurement when clinically indicated
Blood and urine tests may be used to assess associated risk or causes

records.description: Thyroid gland makes too much hormone, causing weight loss, fast heartbeat, sweating, shakiness and irritability.
red_flags: very fast or irregular heartbeat with severe symptoms
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: More common in women; pregnancy needs close care by a Gynecologist and Endocrinologist.
baseline_tests: Thyroid function blood test including TSH and T4/T3 as indicated
Further antibody tests or thyroid imaging when clinically indicated

records.description: Blood sugar that falls too low, mostly in people with diabetes taking insulin or tablets. Causes shakiness, sweating, hunger and confusion.
red_flags: confusion that does not improve after sugar
records.age_notes: Child with diabetes: Pediatrician.
Older adults and people taking blood-pressure medicines may need assessment for postural hypotension.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy can be associated with lower blood pressure and should be assessed in context.
baseline_tests: Blood pressure measurement after changing position when postural hypotension is suspected
Blood tests or ECG if an underlying cause is suspected
records.description: Low blood pressure / hypotension. Common words people use: low blood pressure, hypotension, dizziness on standing, lightheadedness, fainting, BP low, kam blood pressure.
Thyroid gland makes too little hormone, causing tiredness, weight gain, feeling cold, dry skin and constipation.
red_flags: swelling of the neck with breathing trouble
records.age_notes: Newborn or child with slow growth: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: More common in women; ask a Gynecologist if periods are irregular or pregnancy is planned.
baseline_tests: Further thyroid tests based on clinician assessment

records.description: Common long-term gut condition causing cramps, bloating, and diarrhoea or constipation, often triggered by food or stress. No sign of bowel damage.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: More common in women; ask Gynecologist if pain is linked to periods.

records.description: Difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep, leaving you tired and low in energy during the day.
red_flags: loud snoring with pauses in breathing
symptoms suggesting severe sleep apnoea or breathing pauses
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: Sleep study only if sleep apnoea suspected
Sleep study only when another sleep disorder such as sleep apnoea is suspected

records.description: Low red blood cells because of too little iron. Causes tiredness, pale skin, dizziness and breathlessness. Common in women and children.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Women with heavy periods or pregnancy: Gynecologist.
baseline_tests: Stool test for occult blood if advised
Iron studies when iron deficiency is suspected
Further tests guided by the suspected cause

records.description: Yellowing of the skin and eyes caused by too much bilirubin, often from liver, gallbladder or blood problems such as hepatitis.
red_flags: new yellowing of skin or eyes
records.age_notes: Newborn jaundice: Pediatrician urgently.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy-associated jaundice requires prompt medical assessment.
baseline_tests: Additional blood tests and abdominal imaging guided by the suspected cause

red_flags: hot, red, swollen joint with fever
cannot move or bear weight after injury
multiple joints swelling with morning stiffness
records.age_notes: Child with joint pain: Pediatrician.
records.description: Joint pain. Common words people use: joint pain, knee pain, swollen joint, arthritis, jodon ka dard, ghutne mein dard.
Infection that reaches the kidneys, causing fever, shivering, pain in the side or back and urinary symptoms. Needs same-day treatment.
red_flags: vomiting and cannot keep fluids down
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician urgently.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women: urgent Gynecologist or hospital care.

records.description: Hard deposits in the kidney that can cause sudden severe pain in the side or back that spreads to the groin, with blood in the urine and nausea.
red_flags: severe pain not controlled by painkillers
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician or Pediatric Urologist.
records.gender_notes: More common in men.
baseline_tests: Blood tests for kidney function and relevant substances
Ultrasound or CT when clinically indicated

records.age_notes: Older adults and people with heart, kidney or liver conditions need assessment of the underlying cause.
records.gender_notes: Pregnancy can cause oedema, but sudden or severe swelling needs prompt assessment.
baseline_tests: Blood tests for kidney/liver/heart-related causes when indicated
ECG or imaging when clinically indicated
records.source: NHS: Swollen ankles, feet and legs (oedema) - https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/oedema/
records.description: Leg swelling / oedema. Common words people use: swollen ankles, swollen feet, leg swelling, ankle oedema, pedon mein soojan, tangon mein soojan.
Parasite infection spread by mosquitoes causing fever with chills and sweating that come in cycles, headache and body aches. Needs prompt testing and treatment.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician urgently.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women: urgent medical care; contact Gynecologist.
baseline_tests: Further blood tests to assess severity when clinically indicated

records.description: Highly contagious viral illness starting with fever, cough, runny nose and red eyes, followed by a red-brown rash that begins on the face.
records.age_notes: Mostly unvaccinated children: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women should contact Gynecologist urgently if exposed.

symptom_keywords: daane jo dabane se na jayen
records.description: Infection of the lining around the brain and spinal cord. Causes fever, severe headache, stiff neck, light sensitivity and sometimes a rash that does not fade when pressed.
red_flags: rash that does not fade under a pressed glass
baby with bulging soft spot or high-pitched cry
records.age_notes: Babies and young children: urgent Pediatrician or hospital.

records.description: Strong, often one-sided throbbing headache with nausea and sensitivity to light or sound. Attacks can last from hours to 3 days.
red_flags: very high temperature with meningitis symptoms
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. New migraine after age 50: see doctor soon.
records.gender_notes: Migraine may change with periods, pregnancy and hormonal medicines.
baseline_tests: MRI or CT only if red flags
Brain imaging only when clinically indicated

records.age_notes: Children with recurrent or persistent mouth ulcers may need pediatric or dental assessment.
baseline_tests: Blood tests if ulcers are recurrent, persistent or an underlying deficiency/systemic condition is suspected
records.description: Mouth ulcer / oral sore. Common words people use: mouth ulcer, oral ulcer, canker sore, mouth sore, painful ulcer in mouth, munh ka chhala, munh ke chalay.
Joint condition where cartilage wears down, causing pain and stiffness in knees, hips and hands, often worse after activity.
records.age_notes: Mostly adults over 45.
records.gender_notes: More common in women after menopause.

records.description: Feeling of a fast, pounding or irregular heartbeat. Often harmless, but a persistent irregular rhythm such as atrial fibrillation raises stroke risk.
red_flags: very fast heartbeat that does not settle
heartbeat with weakness or speech trouble
records.age_notes: Child with fast heartbeat: Pediatrician.

records.description: Hormone condition in women causing irregular or missed periods, excess facial or body hair, acne and weight gain. Often linked to cysts on the ovaries and insulin resistance.
red_flags: no periods for more than 3 months with possible pregnancy
records.age_notes: Teenage girls: Gynecologist or Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Applies to women only.
baseline_tests: Hormone tests (LH, FSH, testosterone, prolactin, TSH)
Fasting blood sugar and lipid profile

records.description: Swollen veins in or around the anus causing itching, discomfort and bright red blood after passing stool. Often linked to constipation.
red_flags: change in bowel habit for more than 3 weeks
very high temperature with feeling unwell
records.age_notes: Rare in children: see Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Common in pregnancy; discuss with Gynecologist.
baseline_tests: Colonoscopy if age over 45 or red flags
Further examination or tests if the diagnosis is uncertain or bleeding needs another cause excluded

records.description: Lung infection that causes fever, cough, fast breathing and chest pain when breathing in. Can be serious, especially in babies, older adults and people with long-term illness.
red_flags: blue or grey lips or skin
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician urgently. Age 65+: see doctor the same day.
baseline_tests: Blood tests when needed to assess severity or alternative diagnoses

records.description: Pregnancy condition with high blood pressure and protein in urine, usually after 20 weeks. Can cause headache, vision changes and swelling and can be dangerous for mother and baby.
red_flags: sudden swelling of face, hands or feet
records.age_notes: Applies to pregnant women only.
records.gender_notes: Applies to women only.

records.description: Long-term skin condition causing thick red patches covered with silvery scales, often on elbows, knees and scalp. Can come with joint pain.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician or Dermatologist.

records.description: Bite or scratch from a dog, cat or other animal can spread rabies, which is almost always fatal once symptoms start. Rabies vaccine and sometimes immunoglobulin must start as soon as possible after a bite.
red_flags: any bite or scratch from a dog, cat, bat or monkey
bite on face, neck or hands
fear of water or fever after a bite
records.age_notes: Child: urgent Pediatrician or hospital.
baseline_tests: Wound examination and washing with soap and water
Rabies post-exposure vaccine and immunoglobulin as advised by the doctor

records.description: Autoimmune condition causing painful, swollen and stiff joints on both sides of the body, worst in the morning and lasting over an hour.
records.age_notes: Child with joint swelling: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: More common in women.

records.description: Common fungal skin infection causing a red, ring-shaped itchy patch with a clearer centre. Spreads by touch or shared towels.
red_flags: no improvement after 2 weeks of treatment
records.age_notes: Child scalp ringworm: Pediatrician or Dermatologist.

records.description: Skin infestation by tiny mites causing intense itching, worse at night, with a rash often between fingers, wrists and waist. Spreads through close contact.
red_flags: skin becomes red, hot and painful
records.age_notes: Baby or child: Pediatrician. All close contacts and family members need treatment.

records.description: Life-threatening reaction to an infection where the body starts to damage its own organs. Signs include fever or very low temperature, fast breathing, confusion and a fast heartbeat.
red_flags: extreme shivering or severe muscle pain
records.age_notes: Babies, older adults and people with weak immunity are at higher risk.

records.description: Inflammation of the sinuses causing facial pain or pressure, blocked nose and thick discharge. Often follows a cold and usually clears in 2 to 3 weeks.
red_flags: swelling or redness around the eye
records.age_notes: Child with long-lasting symptoms: Pediatrician or ENT.
baseline_tests: CT scan of sinuses only if doctor advises
Clinical assessment of symptoms and nasal/face examination
Further imaging or specialist assessment if persistent, recurrent or complicated

red_flags: swelling of lips, face or tongue
rash that does not fade when pressed
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: Skin scraping or allergy tests (if advised)
records.source: NHS website: Skin rash / Itching - verify
records.description: Skin problem / rash. Common words people use: rash, itching, skin allergy, pimples, daane, kharish, jild par nishan.

red_flags: sore throat lasting more than a week
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
records.description: Throat infection. Common words people use: sore throat, throat pain, pain swallowing, gala kharab, gala dard, gale mein dard.

records.age_notes: Children with significant injuries should be assessed because growth plates can be affected.
records.description: Musculoskeletal injury / sprain or strain. Common words people use: sprain, strain, twisted ankle, muscle strain, swollen joint after injury, bruise after injury, moch aana, moche.

records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Lower abdominal pain in women may need a Gynecologist.
records.source: NHS website: Stomach ache and abdominal pain - verify
records.description: Abdominal pain. Common words people use: stomach pain, abdominal pain, belly pain, pait dard, pait mein dard.
Sore in the lining of the stomach or gut causing burning pain, often related to H. pylori infection or painkiller use.
records.age_notes: Mostly adults.

red_flags: thoughts of self-harm or ending life
hearing or seeing things that others do not
records.age_notes: Child or teen: Child psychiatrist or psychologist if available.
baseline_tests: Basic blood tests to rule out other causes (if advised)
records.description: Mental health concern. Common words people use: anxiety, stress, low mood, depression, panic, cannot sleep, tension, pareshani.
Medical emergency where blood supply to part of the brain is cut off. Signs are face drooping, arm weakness and speech problems. Treatment works best within hours.
records.age_notes: Can happen at any age but risk rises after 55.

records.description: Dull, tight, band-like pain on both sides of the head, often linked to stress, poor sleep, eye strain or skipped meals.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. Frequent headaches in a child need a check.

records.description: Short-lasting stroke-like symptoms that go away within minutes to hours. It is a warning sign and needs urgent hospital check even if symptoms have gone.
red_flags: symptoms that have gone away but happened today
records.age_notes: Mostly adults over 50 or people with high blood pressure or diabetes.

records.description: Painful, red throat, often with swollen tonsils and fever. Most cases are viral and settle in about a week; some need antibiotics.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. Recurrent tonsillitis in children: ENT.
Child: Pediatric Dentist if available.
records.description: Dental problem. Common words people use: toothache, tooth pain, gum swelling, daant dard, daant mein dard.
Bacterial infection that usually affects the lungs. Typical signs are a long cough, weight loss, fever and night sweats. It can be cured with a full course of antibiotics.
red_flags: new weakness or loss of movement
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. Contacts of a TB patient should be checked.
baseline_tests: Rapid molecular diagnostic test when TB disease is suspected
Chest X-ray or other imaging as clinically indicated

records.description: Autoimmune condition where the body cannot make insulin. Starts quickly with thirst, frequent urination and weight loss, mostly in children and young adults.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician or pediatric Endocrinologist.

records.description: Long-term condition where blood sugar stays too high. Common signs are thirst, frequent urination, tiredness, slow-healing wounds and blurred vision.
red_flags: foot ulcer that is not healing
records.age_notes: Mostly adults over 40 but now seen in younger people.
records.gender_notes: Women with diabetes in pregnancy need a Gynecologist and Endocrinologist.

records.description: Bacterial infection spread by dirty food or water. Causes a fever that slowly rises over days, headache, stomach pain and weakness. Needs antibiotics.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: Typhidot or Widal only as supportive tests

red_flags: fever with back or side pain
symptoms in a child or man
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
records.gender_notes: Women in pregnancy should see a doctor promptly.
records.source: NHS website: Urinary tract infections - verify
records.description: Urinary problem (possible urinary infection). Common words people use: burning urine, painful urination, frequent urination, peshab mein jalan, baar baar peshab.
Infection of the bladder or urine tubes causing burning when passing urine, frequent urge, lower belly pain and cloudy or smelly urine.
records.age_notes: Child with UTI: Pediatrician. Men with UTI: see Urologist.
records.gender_notes: Women get UTIs more often. Pregnant women with symptoms need a Gynecologist soon.

records.description: Feeling that you or the room is spinning, often with nausea. Most often caused by an inner ear problem and usually settles in days to weeks.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician.
baseline_tests: Hearing assessment or imaging if clinically indicated

records.description: Very common stomach infection causing sudden vomiting and watery diarrhoea. It spreads easily and mostly clears in 1 to 2 days.
records.age_notes: Child under 5: Pediatrician; use ORS and see doctor early.
baseline_tests: Stool test if blood or long duration

records.description: Viral infection that inflames the liver. Hepatitis A spreads through dirty food or water; hepatitis B and C spread through blood and body fluids. Can cause tiredness, nausea, dark urine and yellow eyes.
records.age_notes: Child: Pediatrician. Newborn of a hepatitis B mother needs vaccination at birth.
records.gender_notes: Pregnant women with hepatitis B or C: Gynecologist and Gastroenterologist together.
baseline_tests: HCV PCR or HBV DNA if positive

red_flags: weakness on one side of the body
records.gender_notes: Heavy periods can cause low iron.
records.source: NHS website: Tiredness and fatigue / Dizziness - verify
records.description: Weakness / tiredness / dizziness. Common words people use: weakness, tiredness, fatigue, dizziness, kamzori, thakan, chakkar.
